clue.text: The trick is to categorise the companion

parts.note: a con is a trick or swindle
to sort things is to put them into categories

explanation.surface: Advice that the secret of success lies in pigeonholing one's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a spouse or partner, especially of a reigning monarch, so a companion in life.

clue.text: Pickets in silhouette?

parts.note: surface reading: striking workers standing at the factory gate; setter's reading: striking pickets are out, standing on the picket line, so the phrase for them doubles as a word for a silhouette

explanation.surface: Striking workers seen as dark shapes against the light.
explanation.walkthrough: Strikers on a picket line are said to be out, and they stand on the line; put those two words together and you have a shape seen only by its edge.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is the contour or edge of a shape, which is exactly what a silhouette shows against a light background.

clue.text: Show indifference by being quiet on the mat

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece written on top of another comes first

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
a rug is a small mat

explanation.surface: Someone sitting silently on a mat, looking unbothered.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrug is to raise the shoulders, a gesture that signals not caring or not knowing.

clue.text: Make allusion about popular distiller

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: to refer to something is to allude to it
something in fashion is popular

explanation.surface: Someone hints at a well-loved maker of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A distiller purifies liquids by heating and condensing them, which is a kind of refining process.

clue.text: Old-style exam turned the heat on old-style forfeit

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: the Certificate of Secondary Education, a British school exam replaced in 1988
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outdated exam made harder, pressing candidates under an outdated penalty system.
explanation.walkthrough: The CSE was a British school-leaving exam before the GCSE took over, hence 'old-style'.
explanation.definitionFit: Escheat was the old legal reversion of land to the lord or Crown when an owner died without heirs, a kind of forfeiture.

clue.text: Philby infiltrates one of his ilk, supplying inadequate cover

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: Philby's kind is a spy
Kim Philby, the British double agent who spied for the Soviets

explanation.surface: A notorious double agent works his way into a spy ring, giving thin protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Kim Philby was the most famous of the Cambridge spies, which makes 'one of his ilk' a spy; 'cover' also plays on a spy's cover story.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing is scanty, revealing too much of the body because there is too little fabric.

clue.text: The man to make adjustments receives greeting from the fitter

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: something that receives takes another item inside itself

parts.note: to alter is to adjust
hi is an informal greeting

explanation.surface: A tailor or mechanic is greeted by the person who fits things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fitter' looks like a tradesman, but here it is the comparative of fit, so HEALTHIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitter as a comparative adjective means in better physical condition, so in better health.

clue.text: Germ-free secret agents up for apprehending part of tribe

indicators.note: apprehending means seizing and holding, so one piece is held inside the other
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the Central Intelligence Agency, the American spy service
a sept is a clan or branch of a tribe, especially in Ireland or Scotland

explanation.surface: Spies arresting a tribesman, oddly described as sterile.
explanation.walkthrough: SEPT is a word for a subdivision of a clan, mostly met in Irish and Scottish history.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from the bacteria and microbes that cause infection, as in a sterile operating theatre.

clue.text: Touring Greece, perhaps, oneÕs purchases include real estate

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: one's shopping is the things one has bought
land is property in the form of ground

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in Greece whose shopping extends to buying property.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'one' stands for 'has', so the numeral is followed by what it has bought, with the property tucked inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Island hopping is travelling from one island to the next, a typical way of seeing the Greek islands, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Commotion in place of confinement

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a fuss or disturbance

explanation.surface: A disturbance breaks out inside a prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is an excited fuss, and in British slang stir is also a prison, a place where people are locked up.

clue.text: Beats American children's game in "Three Sisters"

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the outer word

parts.note: the three Fates of Greek myth, sisters who spin and cut the thread of life
US stands for the United States
tig is the British name for tag, the chasing game

explanation.surface: A review saying an American kids' game outdoes Chekhov's play Three Sisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Three Sisters' is Chekhov's play on the surface but the Fates in the wordplay. Tig is the British word for the playground game of tag.
explanation.definitionFit: To fustigate is a rare, literary verb meaning to cudgel or thrash someone with a stick.

clue.text: Classical mantrap thatÕs never been touched

parts.note: vir is Latin, the classical language, for man
a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned trap for men that nobody has ever sprung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mantrap' must be split into man and trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgin describes anything untouched or unused, as in virgin snow or virgin forest.

clue.text: A couple get put through and cut off

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something put through another passes into its middle

parts.note: to couple animals is to mate them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A phone call: two people are connected, then the line goes dead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put through' and 'cut off' are telephone language on the surface; here 'cut off' is surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: To amputate is to remove a limb surgically by cutting it away from the body.

clue.text: Wild Man of the East in the gallery chasing some Parisian

indicators.note: something chasing follows behind, so this piece comes later

parts.note: des is French for some

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Prado is the great art gallery in Madrid
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: An oriental outlaw causing a scene in an art gallery, pursuing a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless, violent outlaw, typically of the American Wild West.

clue.text: Make declaration, I say, before church

indicators.note: before places this piece ahead of the next in the entry

parts.note: I is an example, say, of a pronoun
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone about to speak in church, opening with 'I say'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' sounds like a speaker's exclamation, but 'say' marks I as an example of a part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce is to announce formally or declare officially, as a judge pronounces sentence.

clue.text: Look hurt when cold drink goes round

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: wine is a drink
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Pulling a face when a chilled drink is handed round.
explanation.definitionFit: To wince is to grimace or flinch briefly, a facial expression of pain or distress.

clue.text: It gives edge to drinks round

indicators.note: turning round makes the word face the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: port is a fortified wine, so ports are drinks

explanation.surface: Buying a round of drinks makes the evening livelier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives edge to' sounds like adding excitement, but the definition means sharpening.
explanation.definitionFit: A strop is a leather strap used for sharpening razors, putting a keen edge on the blade.

clue.text: Casual dress in the turret, maybe

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sleeveless knitted pullover worn informally
second meaning: the uppermost part of an armoured vehicle

explanation.surface: A soldier dressed down, sitting in a gun turret.
explanation.walkthrough: A tank top is a sleeveless sweater; the turret is perhaps the top of a military tank.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment is relaxed knitwear, and the armoured vehicle's upper section, such as its turret, is literally its top.

clue.text: Cleaner copies including past papers

indicators.note: including means taking in, so one piece goes inside the pair

parts.note: cc means carbon copies on a letter
old things belong to the past
a ream is a quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: An office cleaner photocopying old documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like a person; it is a cosmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: Cold cream is an emollient cosmetic used to cleanse the skin and remove make-up.

clue.text: Decline to eliminate odour?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a downward slope or fall

definitions.note: read as de-scent, a coined verb
definitions.meaning: second meaning, whimsical: de- means remove and a scent is a smell

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented word: split as de-scent, it would mean removing a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A descent is a going down or a fall in level or status, so a decline.

clue.text: Best thing to do to the Titanic when thereÕs an orchestra playing

definitions.text: Best thing to do to the Titanic

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, a
a band is a group of musicians
a show that is playing is on

explanation.surface: The famous image of the Titanic's band playing as the liner sank.
explanation.walkthrough: The ship's musicians famously kept playing as the Titanic went down, so the surface is history as well as wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandoning ship means leaving a sinking vessel for good, the wisest course on the stricken liner.

clue.text: China animal given fodder

indicators.note: one piece is given the next, so they are joined end to end

parts.note: a cat is an animal
hay is dried grass used as fodder

explanation.surface: A pet being fed straw from a piece of crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like crockery or a country; it is the old poetic name for the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is the archaic, poetic name for China, used by medieval Europeans such as Marco Polo.

clue.text: Middle bit of Yorkshire-manÕs fish tail?

indicators.note: Yorkshire speech famously clips its words, dropping the final consonant of a short preposition

parts.note: a tail is an end
taken as written
a carp is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Asking which part of a fish a Yorkshireman calls the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: A Yorkshireman says 'end o' carp' for a carp's tail, the dropped f being stereotypical of the dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: The endocarp is the innermost layer of a fruit's wall, such as the stone around a plum seed.

clue.text: Feature of middle age or newspaper

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the thickening waistline of middle years

definitions.note: read as feature of a newspaper
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a feature across two facing pages

explanation.surface: A list of things typical of middle years, including reading the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature of' serves both halves: the middle-age thickening and a double-page article.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle-age spread is the weight gained round the waist in later life; a spread is also a two-page article.

clue.text: Discharge ambassador in peculiar circumstances

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: rum is British slang for odd or peculiar
HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title

explanation.surface: A diplomat sent home under odd circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum here is the dated British adjective for strange, not the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery mucus discharged from the eyes or nose, as with a cold.

clue.text: Five wanting the evensong transposed to a sacred site

indicators.note: transposed means moved into a different order
wanting means lacking, so these letters are removed

parts.note: taken as written
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A church service minus a few voices, moved to an ancient holy place.
explanation.definitionFit: Stonehenge is the prehistoric stone circle on Salisbury Plain, thought to have been a ceremonial or religious monument.

clue.text: Headless donkey in the vortex

indicators.note: without a head means the first letter goes

parts.note: neddy is a British informal word for a donkey

explanation.surface: A decapitated donkey caught in a whirlpool.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is a circular current of water or air, a small whirlpool.

clue.text: BirdÕs better suited to Cartesian co-ordinates

parts.note: apter is the comparative of apt, suited
x and y are the axes of the Cartesian graph

explanation.surface: A bird finds graph paper more to its liking.
explanation.definitionFit: Apteryx is the scientific genus name of the kiwi, the flightless New Zealand bird.

clue.text: Semi-staged, "The Talking Bird" requires staying power

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the word is kept

parts.note: taken as written
the mina or myna is an Asian bird that mimics speech

explanation.surface: A half-produced show called The Talking Bird needs endurance to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Stamina is the physical or mental endurance to keep going over a long effort.
